title: feat: repo diet, read-only reviewers and a risk-based sweep floor
headline: The owner's profile and the third-party backups leave the public kit repo, a sweep reviewer's shell can only read and write its own scratch folder, the sweep floor follows what a diff touches, and the content checks in CI run the base commit's copies.
alignment: v1.44.0 is build 18 of the v2.0 plan: the T10 rest (backups out, one home for process skills, the sweep floor by risk, shared test helpers), K135 part (a), K136 to K141, K143 and K144, I10, and the 35 real findings of its sweep.

items.text: Install reads the owner's profile from `~/.claude/kit-owner-profile.md`, outside the public repo; the repo keeps a blank example, and install refuses rather than blank Owner Context lines it finds with no profile.
items.where: Upgrading the kit with install user
items.before: Profile tracked in the public kit repo
items.after: Profile in the user config folder; a blanking install refused

items.text: The third-party backups move from `vendor/` to a private repo cloned beside the kit, named by `vendor.dir`; the kit keeps `vendor-index.json`, the credits and a hash of each backup.
items.before: About 13 MB of third-party backups in the public repo
items.after: An index of them; the backups in a private repo

items.text: A sweep reviewer's shell runs only known reads (git reads, grep, cat, ls and the like, a script file) and writes only to its own scratch folder, named in full; anything else is refused.
items.where: A sweep reviewer running a shell command
items.before: Brief text asked it to write nowhere else
items.after: Hook refuses all but reads and scratch writes

items.text: The sweep floor follows what the diff touches: gate code (CI and the scripts it runs, hooks, guards, the kit's install) is a feature sweep with security roles; docs, records and moved tests stay triage.
items.before: Line counts and added files decided it
items.after: What the diff touches decides it

items.text: CI's six content checks (scrub, word check, project map, rule map, link scan, build is fresh) run the base commit's copies over the PR's tree, so that job runs none of the PR's code.
[trial] One home for process skills: the kit's own skills; a third-party process skill set stays off, as a credited backup only.
Each Yes in a pop-up of several questions unlocks its own quoted act once; a No still holds its act, and two questions of one text are no yes.
The guards pass a read loop over a glob of guard files, cmp and du; a loop whose names split, set IFS, change folder or cannot be listed is still held.
The PR and release attribution checks read a Requested by line or marker hidden by an HTML comment, over a line break too, or by an empty link inside the word.
From 1.44.0 a build record needs an item naming a where, and the PR body audits need at least one Summary row, with CRLF ends read.
A recall run refuses rule text over its size cap before any session starts, and the scorer names the under-bar rule (decision 7).
The coverage map credits lines run from an installed guard copy to the repo file it came from, placing a filled-in copy's lines right.
The kit's test files share one helper module, `tests/kit-helpers.mjs`, in place of the copies the 1.43.1 split left in each.
README and the recall workflow say the kit repo is public.

verification: The owner's profile and the backups are gone from the tree at this commit; the secret scan over the added lines finds no shape.
The vendor index was written from the private backup clone, with a hash of each backup.
The sweep report audit is clean, and every real finding is fixed in this build.

decisions.decision: A read-only allowlist for the reviewer fence
decisions.why: The owner's pop-up: each review round found a new spelling past a list of write commands, so the fence names what may run instead.

decisions.decision: Install refuses, never copies, a profile left in the kit folder
decisions.why: The profile is never read from the public folder; refusing names the move and keeps the owner's lines.

decisions.decision: The test check's judge split stays a named limit
decisions.why: The owner's pop-up: its results file would come from the job that runs the PR's tests, so splitting it adds no protection now.
Install reads the profile from a new place, the backups move, and the sweep floor changes for every project.

upgrading: Before checking out the 1.44.0 tag, copy the kit folder's `owner-profile.md` to `~/.claude/kit-owner-profile.md` (or print the last copy with `git show v1.43.1:owner-profile.md`), then install user and install project. To snapshot or restore backups, clone the private backup repo into the folder `vendor.dir` names first.
limits: A script a sweep reviewer runs writes past what its command line shows, and which role's scratch folder a write lands in goes unchecked. CI's test check still runs the PR's own tests in its job. Git history before 1.44.0 still holds the old profile and backups.
